category_title: Struggling readers who identify and reject inaccurate speech-to-text transcriptions
student_description: Maggie is a first-grade student who struggles with reading but possesses strong graphosemantic awareness, allowing her to easily spot when speech recognition (SR) software misinterprets her dictation. She is highly motivated to write but becomes frustrated and stalled by inaccurate transcriptions, often skipping the brainstorming phase entirely. She uniquely requires adult dictation to bypass technological failures and metacognitive dialogue to bridge the gap between her oral intent and the written output.

criteria.rationale: Maggie has strong graphosemantic awareness and needs guided dialogue to analyze why the written text does not match her oral intent.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to compare her intended spoken words with the visual representation of the inaccurate transcription (e.g., asking how she knows the text is incorrect).

criteria.rationale: When speech recognition consistently fails, Maggie needs an accurate written model to copy so her writing process is not halted.
criteria.check: The tutor offers to dictate the student's intended sentence into the technology themselves to generate a 100% accurate transcription for the student to copy.

criteria.rationale: Quickly removing inappropriate or highly inaccurate text prevents distress and maintains a safe environment for a student highly sensitive to transcription errors.
criteria.check: The tutor actively intervenes to delete or modify inappropriate or nonsensical transcriptions before or as soon as the student notices them.
